payload.title: AI Builders Daily · 2026-06-06
payload.summary:
**Agent tooling got real teeth**; **Claude Cowork** doubled limits and pushed desktop delegation, while **Vercel** showed storage that survives sandbox lifecycles; **Replit x Shopify** and **Cursor Composer 2.5** both pointed at a simpler path from idea to shipped software; the mood across builders: prompts, memory, and workflow design now matter as much as raw model quality.

**这波更新挺实在**；**Claude Cowork** 直接把额度翻倍，摆明了要你把脏活累活丢给 agent；**Vercel** 把存储从 sandbox 生命周期里拆出来，这一下基础设施味儿就上来了；**Replit x Shopify**、**Cursor Composer 2.5** 都在推一件事：做软件的门槛还在掉，但真拉开差距的，已经不是会不会写提示词，而是你怎么组织记忆、技能和执行链路。

sections.headline: **Figma** says the "SaaS apocalypse" is a goldmine, not a funeral · **Figma** 认为所谓 "SaaS 末日" 更像金矿，不像追悼会
sections.body:
In **AI & I by Every**, **Figma** product leader Matt Colyer argues that AI will explode the number of software creators, not wipe out software companies. His bet is blunt: more people building means more software in the world, which creates more demand for products that handle the boring, painful parts people do not want to run themselves.

He also makes a less glamorous point that lands: vibe-coded prototypes are fun, maintenance is not. Colyer describes building personal agents, including an early email agent for school and PTO overload, then realizing that ownership, upgrades, and reliability are the real tax. That is why he says he buys more software now, not less.

A second thread in the conversation is agent workflow design. Colyer talks about summaries, memory, and proactive delivery as the unlocks that matter in daily use. The hard part is not getting a model to produce text. It is teaching an agent what matters now, what can wait, and what only looks irrelevant until three days later.

在 **AI & I by Every** 这期里，**Figma** 的产品负责人 Matt Colyer 讲得很直白：AI 不会把软件公司一锅端，反而会把软件创作者的数量抬上去。人多了，软件只会更多；而那些帮人扛住维护、稳定性、运营细活的产品，反而更值钱。

他还点破了一个经常被故意略过的现实：把东西糊出来不难，长期养着才烦。Colyer 提到自己早年做过个人 agent，连学校和家长会邮件都拿来自动处理，后来发现真正磨人的不是第一版，而是后面的升级、可靠性和持续维护。所以他的结论不是少买软件，而是现在更愿意付钱让别人来跑这些东西。

还有一条很关键：agent 好不好用，已经不只是模型聪不聪明的问题。Colyer 反复提到总结、记忆、主动推送这些能力。难点不在生成一段话，而在于让系统知道什么事今天该看、什么事可以先放、什么信息现在像噪音，过两天却会变成重点。

sections.headline: Ask the model a question, not an order · 把提示写成问题，别写成命令
sections.body:
a smarter alternative to "always use plan mode": 

always frame your task as a question, so that the model is invited to push back and rate the quality of the idea/suggest alternatives, rather than blindly execute what you SAID to do 

(which is often not precisely what you MEANT)

literally just appending "?" to the end of your prompt often does it

比起 "永远用 plan mode"，更聪明的做法是：

始终把你的任务写成一个问题，这样模型才会被引导来反驳你、评估想法质量、给出替代方案，而不是机械执行你"说了要做"的事。

（而你说出来的，往往并不等于你真正想表达的。）

很多时候，真的只是在提示词末尾加一个 "?" 就够了。

sections.headline: Peter Yang lays out a recipe for self-improving AI skills · Peter Yang 给出一套会自检、会进化的 AI skill 配方
sections.body:
How to build AI skills that check their own work and improve over time:

1. Give it context

Ask AI: "Create a skill for this [repeated task]. Here are examples of good output so it knows what good looks like."

2. Make it easy to trigger

“Write a clear skill description using this pattern: Use when the user wants to [do this].”

3. Add evals

"Create an evals md with 10 pass/fail checks for common errors in the skill's output."

4. Add memory

"Create a memory md to capture one-sentence learnings from past chats using this skill."

5. Build a skill to edit skills

"Create a skill that cleans up other skills by removing duplicate or stale instructions, vague rules, and AI slop."

📌 Watch my full walkthrough here: https://t.co/u434ytNSZd

怎么做出会检查自己工作、还会越用越好的 AI skill：

1. 给它上下文

让 AI："为这个[重复任务]创建一个 skill。这里有一些高质量输出示例，让它知道什么叫好。"

2. 让触发方式足够简单

"按这个模式写一个清晰的 skill 描述：Use when the user wants to [do this]。"

3. 加上 evals

"创建一个 evals md，里面放 10 个通过/失败检查，覆盖这个 skill 输出里常见的错误。"

4. 加上 memory

"创建一个 memory md，用一句话记录过去聊天里使用这个 skill 得到的经验。"

5. 再做一个专门改 skill 的 skill

"创建一个 skill，用来清理其他 skill，删掉重复或过时的指令、模糊规则，还有 AI 味太重的废话。"

📌 完整演示在这里：https://t.co/u434ytNSZd

sections.headline: Build for the slope, not today's model ceiling · 别只盯着今天的模型上限，要按增长斜率来搭
sections.body:
One of the most common mistakes I see enterprise AI teams make is building for today’s model capabilities and price points.

Think 6 months out. Models will be way smarter and cheaper.

Scaffold around today’s model weaknesses to push the frontier. Bet that the next generation of models will natively solve for the scaffold. Push the frontier again.

Build for the slope.

Over time, that ability to repeatedly identify and bridge model gaps becomes a moat of its own.

我看到企业 AI 团队最常犯的错误之一，就是按今天的模型能力和价格来做产品。

把时间往后看 6 个月。模型会更聪明，也会更便宜。

围着今天模型的短板先搭脚手架，把边界往前推。赌下一代模型会原生吃掉这层脚手架。然后你再继续往前推。

按斜率来建，不要按静态点来建。

时间一长，那种反复识别模型缺口、再把缺口补上的能力，本身就会变成护城河。

sections.headline: Even coding agents still need humans, says **Box** CEO · **Box** CEO 说连写代码这件事，agent 也还离不开人
sections.body:
Coding is basically the pinnacle of what you could reasonably automate with AI, and yet we still need human engineers to oversee agents for them to be effective.

The AI models are trained on an incredible amount of sophisticated code. The users are highly technical and can use the latest tools quickly. The work is “verifiable” because you can test an app. The outcomes are often removed from the quality of the code (you can have sloppy code but the app can still work). And the context for the agent is often already digitized and sitting in the codebase. 

That’s an incredible amount of benefits that AI coding agents get to work with. Some of those apply to knowledge work, but most don’t in areas where the work needs to be fully reviewed to be useful, or where data isn’t as abundantly digitized. This makes the job for agents in knowledge work more complicated.

So if with all of that, engineers still remain in very high demand, the risks are going to be less than what’s perceived for other areas of knowledge work. Agents will let people do far more than they did before, but the people don’t go away.

写代码这件事，基本已经算是 AI 最适合自动化的高地了，但即便这样，我们还是需要人类工程师盯着 agent，它们才真正好用。

AI 模型吃过海量复杂代码训练；用户本身技术很强，能很快上手新工具；这类工作还"可验证"，因为应用能测；而且结果常常跟代码本身是否漂亮没那么强绑定（代码写得乱，应用照样可能能跑）；agent 需要的上下文，很多时候也已经数字化，直接躺在代码库里。

这已经是 AI coding agent 能遇到的一整套有利条件了。知识工作里只有一部分条件成立，更多场景不是必须人工完整审一遍才有用，就是数据根本没被这么充分数字化。所以 agent 去做知识工作，难度其实更高。

既然在这种优势拉满的场景里，工程师的需求都还很高，那其他知识工作被替掉的风险，大概率没有外界想得那么夸张。agent 会让人做得更多，但人不会消失。
